findings.title: Misleading user-facing error message for disabled SQL expressions
findings.body: The error message returned when a user submits a QueryTypeSQL is 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. SQL expressions are in fact implemented (stubs in pkg/expr/sql/db.go); they are disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264). Users who try to use the (documented) SQL Expressions feature will see a message suggesting the feature does not exist, when the actual reason is a security disable. The message should explain that SQL expressions are disabled for security, or at minimum say 'disabled' rather than 'not implemented'.

findings.title: Misleading control flow in enableSqlExpressions risks re-introducing CVE-2024-9264
findings.body: The newly added enableSqlExpressions function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but then ignores the computed value: both the `if enabled` branch and the fallthrough return false. The function therefore always returns false regardless of the feature flag. While this currently produces the desired (safe) behavior of always disabling SQL expressions, the structure suggests the gate is conditional and invites a future maintainer to 'fix' the obvious dead branch (e.g. by returning true in one of the paths) which would silently re-enable SQL expressions and re-introduce the RCE/LFI vulnerability that this PR is fixing. The function should be written as an unconditional `return false` with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264, or the unused feature-flag check should be removed entirely.

findings.title: NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand are direct entry points not gated by the new disable check
findings.body: The disable check is only added in pkg/expr/reader.go's QueryTypeSQL case. The exported functions NewSQLCommand (line 25) and UnmarshalSQLCommand (line 51) in this file remain callable from any other caller in the codebase without going through that check. Today this is mitigated only by the fact that the new pkg/expr/sql/db.go stubs return 'not implemented' instead of executing SQL, so no DuckDB-backed SQL is run. This is a defense-in-depth concern: any code path (existing or future) that calls NewSQLCommand or UnmarshalSQLCommand directly will reach the stubbed backend, and a future change that re-implements those stubs to call real SQL would re-introduce CVE-2024-9264 without touching reader.go. The same gate (or an explicit early return with the security error) should be enforced inside NewSQLCommand so that disabling SQL expressions cannot be bypassed by callers that don't use ExpressionQueryReader.

findings.title: New stubbed SQL backend has no tests and may break existing SQL expression tests
findings.body: pkg/expr/sql/db.go introduces a new DB type whose three methods (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) all unconditionally return 'not implemented'. There are no tests added that exercise this file or that assert QueryTypeSQL now returns the expected error in pkg/expr/reader.go. Existing tests in pkg/expr that previously exercised the DuckDB-backed path (or any test that calls NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand or pkg/expr/sql.TablesList) will now fail with 'not implemented' instead of running the real SQL. These tests should be updated to assert the new disabled behavior, or new tests should be added covering the reader.go gating, otherwise a future regression that silently re-enables the vulnerable path could go undetected.

findings.title: TablesList retains DuckDB-style command string even though backend is disabled
findings.body: TablesList still constructs a DuckDB-flavoured command ('SELECT json_serialize_sql(\'%s\')', rawSQL) and calls the stub DB.RunCommands, which always returns 'not implemented'. Because pkg/expr/reader.go now blocks QueryTypeSQL before this code runs, and pkg/expr/sql/db.go stubs out the execution, there is no live vulnerability. However, the DuckDB-specific command string is now misleading dead code that documents a non-existent backend. It should either be removed (since TablesList will always error), or the function should short-circuit with a clear 'sql expressions are disabled' error before formatting any command, matching the user-facing message returned at pkg/expr/reader.go:131.
